name: Mala Liath

attributes.attribute: a Scottish folkloric name for a cailleach who tended a herd of wild pigs
a goddess of wild animals, especially deer, in Ross and Cromary in Scotland
a hag figure, elsewhere a weather divinity or a creator goddess

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mala Liath was a Scottish folkloric figure. In Ross and Cromary in Scotland, the name was given to a cailleach, or hag, who tended a herd of wild pigs. The cailleach appears often in this form as a goddess of wild animals, especially deer. In other lands she is more typically a weather divinity or a creator goddess. She may descend from a pre-Celtic deity. The word cailleach is not derived from any Celtic language. It has, however, been adopted into several as a word for an old woman.
objective: Document Mala Liath, the Scottish cailleach who tended wild pigs.
